correctness.rationale: For an arbitrary admissible list assignment, the proof constructs two singleton witness colors in the first two parts. The second-part list lower bound is at least \(n_1+2\): offset two gives this directly, while offset one uses the existence of a nonempty third part. Every later part has lists strictly larger than the number of colors already used, so it can use a palette disjoint from all earlier parts. This proves properness and preserves both singleton neighborhood witnesses for all vertices. The packaged finite checker replayed the construction on exhaustive small list assignments and deterministic larger stress tests, ending with ALL CHECKS PASSED; those finite checks are implementation tests, not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Complete multipartite graphs are a canonical dense family not subsumed by the sparse maximum-average-degree theorems. The offset-two clause verifies a recent universal conjectural bound throughout this family and strictly extends the proved \(K_{2,r}\) slice. The offset-one clause reaches the stronger conjectural scale for all multipartite graphs with at least three parts and even covers some instances outside the conjecture’s minimum-degree-three hypothesis. The proof exposes a reusable structural mechanism: two singleton witness colors plus disjoint inter-part palettes.
